title: Automation: piece runner, step finisher, benchmarks, gallery branch, manual pages, feature switches
Eyes: the scene drawn as real light (HDR), metered and adapting like eyes, the AgX film curve; Settings → Lighting New/Classic
check: Walk from the bright bar counter to the dark stage corner: the picture slowly brightens as your eyes adjust. Settings → Graphics → Lighting: flip New and Classic, highlights look softer in New.

title: Real units: every lamp in lumens and Kelvin, true inverse-square light with no edge, white balance like eyes; world lights migrated (tools/world_migrate.mjs)
check: Stand at the door: lamp light now spreads across the whole room in soft pools, brightest under each lamp, with no edge where it stops. Bulbs look warm, not orange.

title: Real material brightness: every material measured (tools/albedo_audit.py → assets/models/albedo.json), the ones darker or brighter than anything real moved into real ranges (new lighting); models keep their shapes for rays
check: Look at the bar top and the stage: wood grain, the mahogany's red and the green wall show clearly instead of near-black.

title: Bounced light, the core: still surfaces gathered and simplified, a ray tree, patches, probes, lamp links, bounces (CPU reference, physics test: a white box ends at 5x its direct light); tools/light.mjs, gi benchmark
check: nothing to see yet (the engine side of bounced light; it shows in L1.5)

title: Bounced light in the game: the GPU casts the build rays (looped/gi.h, shaders/gi.wgsl), one more bounce every frame, every pixel reads its 8 probes; the flat fill replaced; no lamp light through walls; debug views; shader check tool
check: After entering, look around for a few seconds: walls and corners near lamps glow softly with bounced light; the arcade's purple spills onto the floor; nothing glows through walls. ?giview=1 shows the bounced light alone.

title: Lights with size: tubes and panels (streak and rectangle highlights, soft area light), lamps fitted to the glowing objects beside them (light tool fit + migration), lamp-backed glow not counted twice in the bounced light
check: Look at the jukebox: its light comes from its whole front and reflects as a soft rectangle on the floor; in the arcade the neon frames light like big soft squares.

title: The new light in the Studio: lumens, colour temperature, shape and size change live; moods in real units (Party brighter, Closing dimmer and warmer)
check: In the Studio, select a ceiling lamp, set Colour temperature to 2000 and Lumens to 1500: the room around it turns amber and brighter at once. Look → Closing dims and warms the bar.

title: The Toolbelt: one list of the engine's tools (toolbelt/tools.json) and one page that opens them (/toolbelt/); the piece runner takes phone pictures of site pages (--pages) and pushes to any branch (--branch)
check: open joshuavelasco.com/toolbelt: three groups (Make, Tune and check, Run by Claude); tap Studio, Dials and Style page, each opens; the search box filters

title: The theme files: every token described once (ui/system/tokens.json: group, kind, what it does), the 4 themes as files (ui/system/themes/), ui/themes.css and looped.js's theme list written from them by tools/uikit.mjs, a check that they agree (quick check and CI); every token's value is unchanged
check: nothing should change: the bar's menus, the Studio and joshuavelasco.com/ui look exactly as before in every theme

title: Screen files and the web renderer: a screen is a tree of parts (ui/system/parts.json lists the 20 kinds and their options), Looped.screen() draws one (ui/screen.js), /ui/screen.html?s=sampler shows every part; uikit checks every screen
check: open joshuavelasco.com/ui/screen.html?s=sampler: keys, choices, knob, fader, meter, save lamps, icons and a see-through panel, all working; add &look=jukebox to see it in another theme

title: The UI Editor (toolbelt/ui-editor/): live preview on top (phone, computer, in game; any theme), the parts list and the inspector below, side by side on a computer; a tap in the preview or the list selects the part in both; its own test
check: open joshuavelasco.com/toolbelt/ui-editor: the sampler in the preview; tap Publish, it gets a dashed outline and 'Key' shows below with its options; tap a row in the list, the preview outlines that part

title: Theme editing in the UI Editor: every token in 6 groups (colour, surfaces, shape, depth, type, lights) with colour pickers that keep see-through, sliders, font and choice menus and the exact text; name, about, light or dark, copy as a new theme, back to as loaded; undo and redo (one step per slider drag); deep links (?mode=theme&group=shape)
check: in the UI Editor tap Theme, then Shape: drag key-r and every key in the preview rounds; Colour: pick a new accent, the preview changes; the undo arrow takes it back
